An improved and attractive local transport company bus system would have the potential of relieving some private automobile travel on the local street system. However, without the existence of a high speed, high capacity freeway system a rubber-tired bus system would be forced to rely on the local street network. If a modified rapid transit system was implemented now it could not use the entire freeway system to the Airport terminal facilities, for a considerable portion of their trip-both distance wise and time vise-would be on surface arterials. Therefore, the bus trip would be considerably longer and would be less attractive. In order for modified rapid transit to compete favorablly with automobile travel it must be fast, efficient and economical. This would not be the case without the Airport Spur freeway. Historical records show that congestion and slow speeds will not encourage mass transit ridership. Rather, transit ridership will be discouraged by delays, inconvenience, detours and the like, and cause further deterioration of transit service.
There will be a negative impact on commercial establishments in the affected areas. It would impact existing streets by increased bus service and concentrating this traffic and turning movements at certain locations. This impact would be significant at 27th and Layton, and at the Layton and Howell Avenues intersections.
Shuttle bus service and satellite parking as provided by Chicago's O'Hare Field was not considered applicable for Mitchell Field. O'Hare is huge and four times the volumes are handled.
